title: Charging station: diagnosis and composition
shows: Two robots share a charging station through an arbiter. Finding why an arbiter is unrealizable (unrealizable core), why a realizable arbiter wins for a bad reason (well-separation), which guarantees are vacuous, and checking the composition of the components with discharge although they feed each other.

steps.note: The core is three guarantees: grant each request in the next step, and never grant both. When both robots request at once the arbiter cannot do both. Show the user these three terms, not the whole contract.
Granting each request eventually (G F (grant | !req)) instead of in the next step lets the arbiter alternate.

Pushy assumes that a robot drops its request after any grant. Granting forever then forces robot 1 never to request again, which breaks the assumption G F req1: the arbiter satisfies its contract without serving anybody. The core is these two assumptions.
Assuming that a robot drops its request only after a grant of that request removes the loophole.
The guarantee G F (grant1 | !req1 | grant2) is removed as vacuous (justice): G F (grant1 | !req1) implies it. Unlike remove_redundant, removing vacuous terms keeps realizability.

The arbiter and the robots feed each other (grant and req). With discharge, the assumptions of the robots on the grants are discharged by the guarantees of the arbiter, in one direction only, so the composite has no assumption left.
A refinement proved on the composition with discharge also holds for the exact composition. If it failed, check again with discharge false before concluding.
